part.text:
Fixed in `lib/helpers/isAbsoluteURL.js:14`.

**Change:** The regex now requires a scheme (`/^[a-z][a-z\d+\-.]*:\/\//i`) instead of optionally matching it, so protocol-relative URLs like `//google.com` are no longer treated as absolute.

**Effect:** `buildFullPath` now combines protocol-relative URLs with the baseURL, so requests stay on the base host instead of being sent to an attacker-controlled one — resolving the SSRF vector in `lib/adapters/http.js:231-232`.

**Validation:**
- All test expectations in `test/specs/helpers/isAbsoluteURL.spec.js` pass (verified manually since those specs run under karma)
- The full mocha unit suite (`test/unit/**`) runs 188 passing, with the SSRF regression test (`test/unit/regression/SNYK-JS-AXIOS-7361793.js`) passing
- The only failure (`should support HTTPS protocol`) was confirmed pre-existing on the unmodified tree (network-dependent timeout), unrelated to this change
